html:
The Rome General Peace Accords were signed on 4 October 1992 in Rome by President Joaquim Chissano and RENAMO leader Afonso Dhlakama, ending the Mozambican Civil War.

Talks had been mediated for two years by the Community of Sant'Egidio, a Catholic lay group, with the Italian government and the church. A United Nations force oversaw the ceasefire and the disarming of both armies.

The first multiparty elections in 1994 were won by FRELIMO, and RENAMO accepted the result. The peace held for two decades, and Mozambique became a model of post-war recovery, though tensions returned in the 2010s and a new deal was signed in 2019 in Maputo.
sum: The Rome General Peace Accords were signed on 4 October 1992 in Rome by President Joaquim Chissano and RENAMO leader Afonso Dhlakama, ending the Mozambican Civil War.
